answer: One concrete Sybil defense is stake-backed unique attestation: each agent must post a locked bond and present a trust signal from a distinct, already-staked attestor before it can earn. Minting a second identity requires a second independent bond and a fresh attestation, so the attacker pays linearly per fake agent. Worse, if any one is caught colluding, slashing triggers a ripple that burns every bond tied to that attestor web, so a whole sparrow farm collapses at once. The cost is real capital at risk, not cheap CPU cycles.
